text:
Aisha: Quick FYI — after last night's canary I'm seeing a persistent tail-latency bump on the reranker embeddings endpoint for non-chat batches. Starts when batching window grows beyond ~1500ms and token_budget hits the floor.
Marco: ugh, thanks. any profiling traces / p99 numbers?
Aisha: p95 ~180ms OK, but p99 jumps from 520ms -> 1.1s. Flame shows lots of kernel stalls during kernel selection and KV cache misses spiking.
Ben: do we have a repro loadshape? non-chat usually has shorter sequences but high qps, right?
Aisha: repro harness: steady 1200 qps, requests of 16-64 tokens, sporadic 512-token outliers. I can drop the harness link: http://ci/redwood/profiles/1941012345
Kira: could be continuous-batcher config overshooting. If early_fill ratio too high we aggregate many small requests and then a big outlier kills the kernel path selection.
Tom: can you paste the current batching policy?
Aisha: current snippet from staging: ```
continuous_batcher:
  max_wait_ms: 1200
  min_batch_size: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  token_budget_per_request: 256
  early_fill_ratio: 0.9
  queue_shard_policy: by_latency
  kv_cache_affinity: false
```
Marco: kv_cache_affinity=false is interesting — without affinity, large outliers push new KV cache pages and thrash. Might explain kernel stalls.
Ben: also token_budget_per_request 256 means once outliers appear, batcher tries to fit a lot of small requests into one kernel exec, increasing sequence variance -> kernel selection chooses the wider execution path (slower).
Eve: Ops ran a micro-deploy earlier to increase batching window to 2s to improve throughput. @ops-bot can you confirm deploy and timing?
ops-bot: deploy r-embed-batcher-2026/patch-14 -> success. Started 2026-07-12T03:12:40Z.
Kira: proposal: make kv_cache_affinity=true for rerank endpoints, lower early_fill_ratio to 0.6, and add token_budget adaptive logic: token_budget = clamp( min( mean_seq_len*1.5, 512 ), 128, 512 ). Also shard queue by seq_bucket (short/med/long).
Marco: agree. shard by seq_bucket will keep outliers from polluting short-batch fast kernel path. Add a soft timeout for long sequences so they don't starve short bins.
Tom: small experiment plan: A) set kv_cache_affinity=true B) early_fill_ratio=0.6 C) add seq_bucket_shards=3 with soft_timeout_ms=[200,800,2000] D) run 1h canary against prod traffic replay.
Aisha: running A+B now on staging. Starting load replay in 3m. will post p95/p99 after 30m.
Ben: also enable detailed kernel_selector logs at DEBUG for the canary window — we need to see which kernels get chosen per batch. Keep sampling low volume to avoid noise.
Aisha: turned on kernel_selector debug (sampling 0.5%). Patch applied.
ops-bot: canary traffic replay job #582 -> running.
Aisha: 30m check-in: p95 steady 175ms, p99 down to ~610ms (was 1.1s). kernel_selector logs show preference for narrow-kernel for short/med buckets. KV miss rate dropped ~38%.
Kira: promising. let's run the full 1h and then test with a synthetic outlier burst to ensure long bucket isolation.
Eve: if this holds, we should roll to prod but gate with automatic rollback if p99 > 900ms for >5m. Also add a perf regression alert tied to kernel_selector error rates.
Marco: I'll draft the rollout config and rollback SLO.
Tom: small follow-up: consider adding an adaptive early_fill that decays when kv_miss_rate rises above threshold. Might automate recovery without manual rollback.
Aisha: noted. I'll open a follow-up RFC for adaptive early_fill and token_budget control. For now, keeping changes minimal to observe effect.
Ben: thanks — great cross-team work.
Aisha: TL;DR: patching kv_cache_affinity=true + lower early_fill + seq_bucket sharding reduced p99 by ~45% in staging; kernel choice stabilized and KV miss rate fell. Will post final numbers after canary completes. :thumbsup:
